sentences.text: The UK has agreed the deals in a bit to cut red tape for British companies The UK will pay a "participation fee" to the EU as part of the deals agreed by Andy Burnham, according to legal documents.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The surcharge will go towards the running costs of EU agencies and systems required to deliver two of the agreements unveiled by the prime minister last week.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: It will be paid in addition to a contribution towards costs that broadly mirrors how EU members contribute to the bloc's shared budget, the documents show.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The government has sought to contrast the financial costs of the deals against their overall effect on the economy, which it estimates will receive an eventual boost by billions a year due to increased trade.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The government is yet to publish an estimate of overall additional costs, but officials said they expected them to be in the low tens of millions per year and "massively outweighed" by predicted economic gains.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: British ministers had already said they were prepared to pay towards administrative costs required to implement deals to re-link the UK to the EU's carbon trading regime, and align Britain with the EU's food standards.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: Now, details of how the payments will be calculated have been revealed in treaties to deliver the two agreements, which are meant to take effect during 2028.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: Legal text for a third agreement agreed last week, on youth visas for 18 to 31 year olds, is expected to be published in the coming days.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: According to the treaties, the payments will be made as a share of the running costs of three EU agencies, as well as various systems that will be used to implement the food standards and emissions deals.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The bulk of the payments, to be made in euros, will come in the form of an "operational contribution" in proportion to the size of the British economy compared to that of the EU.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: This broadly mirrors the way in which EU member states split the cost of their main contributions towards the bloc's overall budget.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: But in addition, the UK will also pay a "participation fee" set at 4% of its main contribution figure.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The government has pointed to the 2021 Brexit trade agreement negotiated by the Conservatives, which also applied an additional surcharge to UK contributions towards the cost of relevant EU programmes.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: However, any additional contributions are likely to be seized upon by opponents of the latest deals.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: Ministers had declined to enter into specifics of the fees during negotiations on the treaties.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: On Sunday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the latest deals agreed by Burnham were "not about cost to the taxpayer".
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: It comes as the government published separate legislation granting it broad powers to incorporate new EU laws required to implement the agreements, without having to hold a full vote each time.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The food standards deal in particular will mean Britain will have to align with scores of current EU food-related laws that have been updated since Brexit, along with future rules in these areas.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The government argues the new powers are required because it would be impractical to run a full parliamentary process each time UK legislation needs to be updated to make the agreement work.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: But it has prompted criticism from opposition parties, because the UK no longer has voting rights at the EU to shape European legislation.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The government argues the UK will get a say on new rules, with the treaty texts confirming British experts can be consulted when new EU laws are being drawn up, with the UK granted "observer" status in certain meetings.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: But Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Burnham was showing "disdain for the democratic process" by asking for a "blank cheque to install and enact EU law".
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: "The prime minister is telling MPs to hand him extraordinary powers whilst having no idea what the EU will actually agree to," she added.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has argued the Burnham's deals would take Britain back into "much of the European Union's single market".
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: He added: "European economies are not growing as fast as ours.
sentences.article_title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals

sentences.text: The idea that getting closer to the EU will mean growth for us is a myth." New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause Badenoch challenges Burnham over university fees for EU students

sentences.article_title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly sentenced over attack on UK couple

sentences.text: Lenacapavir has received WHO's approval for HIV prevention Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.

sentences.text: The drug, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection and is expected to cost just $40 (£30) per person annually.

sentences.text: The Fender Stratocaster is widely considered to be the best-known shape in electric guitars Hans Thomann leads the way through his music store in central Germany to the large electric guitar department, where the walls are hung with hundreds of instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Brands on show include famous names Fender and Gibson, plus Harley Benton.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The latter is a low-price range of guitars owned by the family-run company that Thomann leads – Thomann, one of the world's largest online retailers of musical instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The shop, together with warehouses and offices, are at the company's headquarters in the tiny village of Treppendorf in rural Upper Franconia, in Bavaria.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The business was founded by Thomann's father, Hans Thomann Senior, in 1954.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In one corner of the store, a young man is trying out a Fender Stratocaster, one of the world's most iconic electric guitars.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Designed in the US in the early 1950's, the "Strat" became the instrument of choice for many famous rock and pop musicians, such as Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton and Buddy Holly.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Hendrix famously set one on fire at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967, and his performances helped make the guitar a symbol of modern rock music.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Hans Thomann says that Fender's letter came as a big surprise These days, the Stratocaster is very much on Hans Thomann's mind, because it's the subject of an intense copyright dispute.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: When the guitar was first made, California-based Fender did not trademark the body shape.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: So, since the 1960s Strat-shaped guitars have been made and sold around the world by countless manufacturers.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The shape is so ubiquitous that many musicians consider it to be a generic design.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: But since March of this year, Fender has begun a new campaign to defend its right to the guitar's sinuous shape.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: It follows a decision by a court in Düsseldorf last December which granted Fender copyright protection , external of the Stratocaster design in Germany.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The defendant, Chinese seller Yiwu Philharmonic Musical Instruments, did not appear.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The Düsseldorf court accepted Fender's arguments and ruled in its favour.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: According to German law the court makes its decision based on the facts presented by the plaintiff if the defendant doesn't raise objections.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The ruling said that Fender's design for the Stratocaster was "an outstanding, free creative achievement" that "clearly reflects the personality of its author".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: It described the guitar as "a body without edges" with "soft curves that evoke associations with the female torso consisting of hips, waist and arms".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: On its website, Fender announced in March , external the decision created "enforceable rights" against any guitars using the Strat body shape, that are manufactured, sold or distributed into Germany or other EU countries, "regardless of where those guitars are produced".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Fender began to send out cease and desist letters to dozens of retailers and manufacturers, both large and small, asking them to stop making and selling Strat lookalikes heading for Europe.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: One of these letters, seen by the BBC, said Fender "insists that you immediately stop manufacturing, marketing, selling and producing the infringing products".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The letter also demanded that companies recall and destroy the guitars.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Jimi Hendrix helped to make the Fender Stratocaster famous The move caused an outcry in the guitar world, among manufacturers and musicians.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Time to boycott Fender," one person wrote on the Facebook page of the boutique US guitar maker, LSL Instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Thomann received a cease-and-desist letter shortly after a visit to Treppendorf in March by Fender's chief executive Bud Cole.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "We remember the meeting as a very positive and constructive exchange," says Thomann.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "At the time we had no indication that Fender was considering legal action." The letter, he says, came as a shock.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "For more than 70 years, we have carried Fender instruments with great appreciation for the brand and many of us are Fender players ourselves.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: We were therefore surprised and disappointed by Fender's recent actions." In 2025, Thomann sold over 112,000 Strat-style guitars, including more than 16,000 made by Fender and Fender subsidiary brand Squier.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "As a retailer, we want to continue offering our customers everything that is available in the world of guitars," adds Thomann.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Thomann says that the Düsseldorf ruling was simply a default judgement based on missed deadlines and didn't represent a "comprehensive review of the legal claims".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: For its part, Fender, which is majority-owned by Hawaii-based company Servco Pacific, says it has a responsibility to protect the Stratocaster's iconic design.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In July, it sued Thomann in a German court, for copyright infringement.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In a statement to the BBC, Fender said it remained "confident" in the original Düsseldorf court judgement.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Our preference has always been to keep lines of communication open and resolve these matters through constructive dialogue rather than litigation," it added.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: With the legal cases continuing, Thomann says he believes it is important to get "legal clarity – not only for us but for the wider guitar industry." "Ultimately, we want to help preserve an environment in which innovation, diversity and creative development can continue to thrive," he adds.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The Stratocaster is the most used emoji for a guitar Thomann says he was taking legal action not just for his company, but for smaller music companies too.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "We used to be a small music shop ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Many of the smaller manufacturers, guitar makers and dealers affected simply don't have the financial and legal resources to conduct a legal dispute like this." One such company is LSL Instruments, a family-owned boutique guitar maker in California.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Its director of sales, Johny Miller, told me that when they first received Fender's letter they were "pretty terrified and blown away".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "They were asking us to retrieve guitars from dealers out there and destroy them and send them proof.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "So when we heard Hans Thomann got the same letter and responded by suing them… so that everybody in the guitar community could understand exactly what's going on… we were so thankful and grateful," he says.

sentences.text: Sophie Hope's credit score was hit by identity fraud Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It turns out, the Brighton-based nail technician and content creator, had been the victim of identity fraud.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Someone had opened accounts in my name across various catalogue sites and ordered multiple items, including a PlayStation 4 and Nike socks," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Without me knowing, the debt was transferred to a secondary finance company.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It spent three to four years accumulating in the background.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was only when I went to apply for a mortgage that I discovered how severely it had dragged down my credit score," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores are "backward looking" says Funmi Olufunwa Hope's experience shows how crucial a credit score can be, but, as in her case, it does not tell the full story.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "As a nation, we are overly obsessed with credit scores," says Funmi Olufunwa, a consumer finance lawyer and founder of financial education business, Hoops Finance.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Three firms - Experian, Equifax and TransUnion - produce credit scores in the UK, and they all work from roughly the same data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "A credit score is backward looking.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It's looking at what has happened in the past, which doesn't necessarily predict the future," says Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "But when somebody's looking to lend you money, they're looking at what actually is affordable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Traditional credit scoring systems also disadvantage "thin-file applicants" - young people and recent immigrants to the UK who won't have built up a credit history.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But with more financial data available than ever before - and a growing appetite for AI to make sense of it - could artificial intelligence help lenders work out who is safe to lend to?
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In the US lending decisions will often hinge on a credit score from a company called FICO, which uses data from the big three credit assessment firms.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But AI-powered lending firms, Upstart and Zest AI have both built businesses which offer lenders an extra option when it comes to assessing a client's credit worthiness.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Thanks to our machine-learning models that look at more than 2,500 variables, we believe we can make significantly more loans at low prices to borrowers from every demographic group," Upstart said in statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But like with many other applications of AI into everyday life, there are concerns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Consumers need to understand what information is being used to make decisions about them, and they need to be able to challenge something when it is wrong," Tucker explains.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores have been a contentious topic for decades for this very reason, says Sandra Wachter, professor of Technology and Regulation at the University of Oxford.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We are not assessing if past decisions were right," Wachter argues, adding, AI does not know about existing social inequalities that impact decisions and could just "replicate what it has seen in the past".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: While companies like Upstart and Zest AI see technology as a tool for financial inclusion, Wachter believes that real transformation requires accountability, as well as automation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: She stresses that firms must apply existing regulations and establish new guardrails to ensure that AI does not simply perpetuate the biases of the past.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Not putting any safeguards in place will fortify, foster, and enhance discrimination." Upstart says it is tackling that issue.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We've invested in creating objective, automated evaluations to identify bias, and we've incorporated those evaluations into our model training process so it evolves to become even more accurate and more fair over time," the company said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Evangeline Atkinson (left) and Laura Mills co-founders of Noggin HQ Evangeline Atkinson had a frustrating experience over her credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "I was at university, paying rent, paying bills, as I had been doing for many years.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: I tried to get a £30-a-month phone contract, and they said no," she recalls.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I dug into it, it was because I was completely invisible to the system.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: No record could be found for me at any of the big three credit reference agencies." That experience inspired her to try to change the system.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: The budget for a government communications team which uses social media ads and influencers to reach the public has almost doubled since Labour came to power.

sentences.article_title: Government set to double spending on social media unit to £25m

sentences.text: It shows the unit's headcount has doubled too, from 21 employees last October to 43 today, as the government speeds up the shift towards digital communications.
sentences.article_title: Government set to double spending on social media unit to £25m

sentences.text: The UK could be included in the EU's proposed scheme to protect car manufacturing in Europe without Britain having to impose import taxes on Chinese electric cars, under draft plans.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: The proposal has been drawn up by Ireland, which currently holds the EU's rotating presidency, and will be discussed by EU governments.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: It comes after previous suggestions the EU would demand the UK align its tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles as a condition of joining the scheme.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: Senior figures in the British government have been talking increasingly positively about the potential to join on terms London would be willing to sign up to, and are cautiously optimistic about this latest move.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: The "Made in Europe" scheme, known formally as the Industrial Accelerator Act, aims to protect EU manufacturing with restrictions on goods from outside countries, with a particular focus on both China and the car industry.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: The idea is potentially dangerous to the UK, as being outside the EU would mean being exposed to restrictions principally intended for others.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: Germany and France had previously agreed a joint position under which UK involvement would have been conditional on matching EU import restrictions and tariffs on imports of Chinese electric cars and hybrids.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: Alignment in this area with the EU would increase the price of increasingly popular Chinese cars in the UK, as well as raising the prospect of a potential Chinese retaliation with its own tariffs imposed on British-made cars.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: Now Ireland, as first reported by the Financial Times , external , is suggesting the UK could join Made in Europe without the need to match the EU's tariffs.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: The argument made in favour of this is the UK and EU car industries are so heavily integrated and interdependent.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: The proposal, which would also apply to Switzerland and countries in the European Economic Area (EEA) such as Norway, would depend on the non-EU countries granting the EU access to their subsidy and procurement schemes.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: However, the idea is still at its early stages.
sentences.article_title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme

sentences.text: It will first be discussed by EU ambassadors, before it is considered by competition ministers from the EU's member states at a meeting next month.

sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology." sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe has a strong position in photonics research.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.

sentences.text: The main disability benefit in England and Wales should be more closely linked to the additional costs claimants face, a government-commissioned review has recommended.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The review on personal independence payment (Pip) led by Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms said the current system was "not appropriate" for claimants who do not have any extra costs arising from their condition.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has committed to some of its recommendations, including fast-track payments for people with severe conditions, but will not respond fully to the plans until early next year.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the year-long review was a "compete farce" and showed a "complete absence of substance".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately added: "All we have is a report that tinkers around the edges of a failed system".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Pip is available to people with long-term physical or mental health conditions who have difficulty doing every day tasks, regardless of whether they work, and it is not linked to income or savings.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The number of people claiming Pip in England and Wales has roughly doubled since 2019 to around four million.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Timms review was set up last year by Sir Keir Starmer's government after his aborted attempt to cut welfare spending, which was derailed by the threat of a rebellion by Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It was co-produced with groups representing disabled people, who had a role in drafting the report.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit Giving a statement in the House of Commons, Sir Stephen said Pip "remains a vital source of support" but the system was "no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: He told MPs the current assessment process was "dehumanising" and focused on "what somebody cannot do", rather than "supporting independence".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has committed to a recommendation that people receiving end-of-life care or with "serious, well-evidenced conditions" would receive payments without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It has also agreed to reduce "unnecessary" reviews for people whose conditions are lifelong or unlikely to improve.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Under the report's proposals, cash payments would remain alongside better support to signpost people into education or employment, although claimants could choose to exchange part of their payment for practical services instead.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: In the longer-term, the report recommends changes to the assessment process that look at someone's real-life additional costs and individual needs, focusing on "how people can live the life they want to live, rather than what they cannot do".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It proposes "improved" questions to understand the extra costs people face, although claimants would not be asked to calculate their costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Currently eligibility for Pip is based on how difficult people find carrying out everyday tasks, with two levels of payment available.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: But the review suggests future payment options could include bands more closely linked to extra costs.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The report says its approach is likely to lead to a "rebalancing" of payments, indicating that some claimants could lose out under a new system, either receiving less than they do currently or not qualifying for payments at all.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: "Those with the highest additional costs, and so the most significant needs, should receive the most support," it says.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: "Conversely, this benefit is not appropriate for those who do not incur any additional costs associated with being disabled." The review also calls for an increase in face-to-face assessments, which has been show to reduce eligibility.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The remit of the review was not to produce savings, and it does not set out whether the reforms would reduce the overall welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Spending on Pip is set to be about £32bn this financial year, a figure projected to rise to £41.5bn by the end of the decade.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It comes after a separate review by former minister Alan Milburn into young people not in education, employment or training (Neets).
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government welcomed Milburn's report , which included a recommendation to move under-25s off Pip and the health element of universal credit, and onto an entirely new benefits system.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: This has led to concerns about a two-tier system, where some people with the same conditions could get different levels of payments depending on their age.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has said it will consider the Timms review alongside Milburn's recommendations, with its final proposals set out early next year.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Sir Stephen said this would include detailing the overall costs of changes to the system.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Eduin Latimer, senior research economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies think tank, said the review's recommendations had "the potential to better tailor Pip to claimants' needs".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: But he said this would also create challenges, "most importantly in defining what disability-related costs are included, and finding a fair way of measuring them".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Latimer said making it easier to apply for Pip in its current form would "likely increase the number of claimants - and hence spending".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: However, they have said any changes should not leave disabled people financially worse off.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats said younger disabled people would now face "months of uncertainty" whilst the government considers the separate reviews from Timms and Milburn, and urged ministers to say quickly what they intend to do.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The disability benefit system is devolved in Scotland and will not change in line with England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: However, the Timms Review could impact the funding the Scottish government receives.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Disability benefits are also devolved in Northern Ireland, but in practice it reflects any changes made to the system in England and Wales.

sentences.text: The previous occupant of Ryua's apartment, pictured here, sadly took their own life From the moment Ryua first walked into her rental apartment in Tokyo she believed it to be haunted.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "When I visited the place for a viewing there was a man standing there, glaring at me," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "Since the estate agent couldn't see him, I realised he must be a ghost." While someone more squeamish would probably have quickly left the flat never to return, Ryua chose to go ahead and move in.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "I'm a bit of a contrarian, so I decided I wanted to become friends with this glaring male ghost," adds Ryua, who works as an aidoru, a young entertainer, and who doesn't wish to share her surname.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Four years later, and still in the same apartment, she says she continues to experience paranormal activity on a daily basis.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: She says she hears endless footsteps and the ghost talking.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Ryua says that she shares her Tokyo apartment with a ghost Although Japan has increasingly marked Halloween , external in recent years, many Japanese people take ghosts seriously all year round.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: The country has a word, "yuurei", which means a lingering, troubled spirit.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: These are the ghosts of people who died in violent or tragic circumstances - those who were murdered, killed themselves, or simply were lonely and died alone.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: If they died at home, then the belief is that their yuurei won't go away.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: For house hunters who are not superstitious or squeamish it means there are big bargains to be found.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: There is a whole category of dwellings called jiko bukken, which means "stigmatised" or "incident" properties.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Under guidelines issued by the government in 2021, Japanese estate agents must disclose suicide, murder, death by fire, and any death where the body was not discovered for an extended period of time.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: For rental properties this information must be disclosed for three years, and it must be revealed indefinitely for any property offered for sale.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: By contrast, in the UK there is no legal requirement to reveal that a person died in a property.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: And in the US, it differs from state to state. , external For example, in California you have to reveal if a person has died in the property in the past three years, while in Arizona and Oregon you do not.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Ryua was told that a man had killed himself in her apartment.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: It meant that she gets an almost 30% discount on her rent on her tiny, 25 sq m bedsit in the fashionable ward of Setagaya.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: She says she pays 45,000 yen ($285; £213) a month, instead of what should have been 62,000 yen.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: While a house where there had been a murder or suicide would probably be harder to sell or rent out anywhere in the world, Tokyo estate agent Erik Oskamp says that Japanese people are particularly superstitious and averse to stigmatised properties.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "[Even] an apartment next to a cemetery will be difficult to rent out, especially if you can see the tombs from the kitchen," explains Oskamp.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "The worst thing is if a suicide has happened in the apartment.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Even if somebody has jumped from the roof, many renters will move out.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Other issues are a serious crime or a lonely death." The latter issue, that of a person dying alone, would not generally affect the price of a property in, say, the UK or the US.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: But in rural Kagoshima, in Japan's southwest, it enabled Diane Tincher to buy a large three-bedroom house for about half of what would have otherwise been the asking price.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: The 69-year-old American has lived in Japan for nearly 40 years, working as a tour guide.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: She says that the estate agent had been straight with her – there was a heavy discount as an elderly lady had died alone, thereby stigmatising the property.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: "I don't believe in ghosts.

sentences.text: A review of the main disability benefit has recommended an overhaul of the system to allow disabled people to "achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report proposes both short and long terms changes to the personal independence payment (Pip) for claimants in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The benefit is claimed by four million people and is available to people whether they are in work or unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Its aim is to help with the additional costs of being disabled.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Pip benefit system 'not fit for purpose' and 'dehumanising' assessments should change, review finds - follow live This is the first review of the benefit since it was introduced in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: More than 40,000 disabled people engaged with the process with more than 90% of them saying they'd had a negative experience while applying for Pip, describing it as stressful, dehumanising or psychologically damaging.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review concludes the Pip process is "not fit for purpose" and calls for a fundamental redesign.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review was chaired by Sir Stephen Timms, the disability minister, the experience of disabled people is clear throughout the review.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A fast-track process should be introduced for two types of claimants.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those with terminal illnesses should get the fastest route to an award to ensure their lives are as comfortable as possible.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those who have severe conditions that are well-evidenced and unlikely to change over time, and whose impact on daily living is clear, should also receive the benefit without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Any subsequent review should avoid unnecessary reassessments.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Other claimants will have to go through an updated initial assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This will examine how a person's condition affects their daily life – functions, barriers, and needs that are currently not being met.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This assessment will determine entitlement to the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will also decide the level of cash award, which will remain the bedrock of the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Optional referrals to support services should also be offered but this will be voluntary and a refusal to engage with them should not affect the benefit level.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A new set of questions should be developed to better understand the extra costs a person faces, but will not ask them to calculate costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The system should recognise fluctuating and cumulative needs and produce decisions that are consistent and be robust against misuse.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The 28-day hospitalisation rule – which sees Pip payments suspended if someone spends more than 28 days as an inpatient – should also be reviewed as claimants find it can cause unnecessary stress and can delay discharges from hospitals.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The inquiry was not set up to find savings in the system despite the fact that spending on Pip is forecast to cost more than £40bn by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In the year before the Covid pandemic, Pip cost £16.3bn when adjusted for inflation to today's prices.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report acknowledges that since the benefit was introduced, the number of people receiving disability benefits has increased across every age group for both men and women.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Most of the increase has happened between 2019 and 2024, with the sharpest increases among young people aged 16-19, people in their 30s and women, whose rates of benefit receipt have risen faster than men's.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report says that a reformed Pip system that more accurately reflects peoples' needs will likely mean "a rebalancing process".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review didn't set out to make savings, it couldn't increase the overall costs and with some people likely to gain, others will almost certainly lose some cash.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review is not explicit on who these people might be.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Separate research last month from a think tank, the Resolution Foundation, suggested that one in six Pip recipients didn't have any additional costs associated with their conditions.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In an interview to coincide with the review, Timms said that "if people don't have extra costs, then this is not the benefit for them".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Alan Milburn's report - which proposed widespread changes to help get young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) into work across the UK - recommended that Pip be removed from people under 25 as part of a package of measures to tackle youth unemployment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Today's review does not make the same recommendation.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will be up to the government to decide how they marry the two reports.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: They have said they are committed to reforming the Pip assessment process, but what that means in practice probably won't be known until the New Year when they publish their considered response.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The work of Andy Burnham's new Number 10 North office in Manchester has been kept largely away from the headlines since it opened in July.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: But the officials based there are mainly focused on two soon-to-be-published documents that could go on to define his time as prime minister.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: The first is Burnham's 10-year plan, which is due next month, and which the prime minister says will lay out a path "to where I believe we all want Britain to be".
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: The second is the 'rewiring the state' white paper, a detailed policy document that will follow in the new year and should give the clearest indication yet of what power Burnham hopes to move away from Westminster to other parts of the country.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: But despite Burnham insisting his new Manchester team will be the "engine room" of change, others in government question how much difference they can really make.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: There's talk among Labour MPs that the 10-year plan, which has also had significant input from Westminster departments, will not go as far as the prime minister had hoped.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: But one official who has seen elements of the plan said it will be "pretty weighty" and include "quite a lot of radicalism".
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Number 10 North has been focused on how the plan can deliver on Burnham's pledge to achieve "growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: One major theme is expected to be reindustrialisation, with advisers exploring how to attract businesses to less prosperous towns and cities.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Staff in Manchester are also said to be looking at what parts of the country may not see growth through reindustrialisation – such as some rural and coastal areas – and what the alternative offer for those places could be.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Eyebrows were raised in Whitehall this summer when a government statement said that "local economic growth policy" would be transferred "from HM Treasury directly into No 10 North".
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Some saw that as an attempt to disempower the Treasury, but sources there insist that no serious decisions on growth can be made without the department's involvement and approval.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Burnham's Number 10 North goes on multi-million pound hiring spree 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy When Burnham first announced plans for the Manchester base, he singled out housing as an issue on which it would take the lead.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: In a speech last month Number 10 North's deputy director highlighted health, transport and education as other areas it was focused on.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: While it's understood the 10-year plan is likely to include long-term ambitions for social care, skills training and council housebuilding, there are doubts within government departments about exactly how involved Number 10 North will eventually be in those areas.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: One Whitehall official said "most things" that have been announced as Number 10 North priorities have in practice "stayed with other departments".
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: They said Number 10 North is "not doing delivery" because it "doesn't have its own resource" and is "underpowered compared to departments" in London.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: A recent hiring spree will see around 120 officials and advisers working from Number 10 North when it moves into its permanent premises next spring.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: That is almost half of the around 280 staff members that work for "Number 10 South", a term some advisers are now using for Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: But even those staffing levels are only a fraction of the numbers employed by other departments.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: The Treasury's north of England campus in Darlington, which was set up in 2021, has around 3,000 staff.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: John Healey is said to have been particularly impressed with the Darlington campus's record of hiring people who would otherwise not have joined the civil service, something Downing Street hopes to achieve in Manchester too.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Darlington's most senior civil servant, Beth Russell, has been working with Number 10 North to share her experience of how best to set up a new government office outside London.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Prime ministers have for decades been frustrated by how little power Number 10 can sometimes wield within Whitehall, arguing that levers can be pulled but nothing then happens.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: One question at the heart of the Number 10 North project is whether it will eventually wield genuine power itself or merely decide which powers to take from Westminster and give to mayors and other regional politicians around the country.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: A government source said Number 10 North's current role is "more in convening" people from elsewhere and argued the prime minister would need to choose what he wanted it to do in the future.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: They added: "I could see it going two different ways.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: "Will it be more delivery or will it be more in the conventional role of Number 10?
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: England currently has 14 metro mayors, a number which is likely to be expanded in the coming years.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Sources in both Number 10 and the Treasury say "fiscal devolution" will be a major part of the Burnham agenda.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: People close to the prime minister say that is likely to ultimately mean more cash-raising, spending and borrowing power for mayors.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Two of Burnham's early announcements this summer saw mayors given a share of income tax and the ability to introduce a tourist tax for people visiting their areas.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: The Treasury believes one of the most underreported elements of Healey's Budget last month was a £1.5bn borrowing facility that will be given to mayors from 2028.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: Sources say that in the future projects such as Doncaster-Sheffield Airport, which Healey gave his backing to, could be given the financial go-ahead directly by mayors, without the need for a separate thumbs up from the chancellor.
sentences.article_title: No 10 North will face greater scrutiny as Burnham's 10-year plan looms

sentences.text: CT scans before (left) and after treatment with daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy (gemcitabine and nabpaclitaxel) showing multiple tumours that are no longer visible.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Yellow arrows indicate the tumours visible before treatment Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades - a daily pill that appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat cancers.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer became undetectable on scans in one in 12 of the patients given daraxonrasib along with chemotherapy in early medical trials.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 participants who had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: But doctors stress it is unclear how long it might keep the disease at bay and should not be seen as a cure.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer Research UK called it "the biggest leap forward in decades" for pancreatic cancer patients.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The charity's Dr Sam Godfrey told BBC News that the results were incredibly exciting.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "What this new drug has done is it's found a way of drugging the undruggable.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are finally seeing progress in pancreatic cancer which is so long overdue." Pancreatic cancer is notoriously hard to treat and has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Although chemotherapy can shrink tumours a bit, the cancer often grows again.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Most patients with advanced disease survive months, not years.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Doctors hope the new treatment might offer patients more time, even if it cannot stop cancers for good.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The trial followed patients for a year and a half, on average, and some did not see their cancer return during this time.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival," he said.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Daraxonrasib is a targeted inhibitor treatment that has already been approved in the US .
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: It works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations, called RAS , external , found in most pancreatic cancers that drive tumour growth.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dozens of other cancers, including lung and ovarian, can have similar mutations, meaning the drug might help lots of other patients too.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dr Godfrey said: "I would hope that the early success that we are beginning to see in pancreatic cancer can also be rolled out to other cancers." He said longer trials and results were vital.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "We really don't think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don't work.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people's digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing." Participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: People with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, will also be included, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Groups have been set up at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Online forum Reddit and a digital rights group are currently involved in a high court battle in the country, arguing that the law change is unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: There have also been reports of Australian teens finding ways to get round the ban - with the UK government promising to make sure tougher blocks are in place.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health
