sentences.text: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the  details public, but has said it will not delete the information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the release of personal information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again." The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the error.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident." Clarification 20 November: This article was amended on 19 November to remove references to the information being 'leaked'.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information was mistakenly disclosed by the GMC in response to a media request.

sentences.text: Marwa was pregnant and new to the UK when her father died in Egypt We're all going to die - and whether we think about it consciously or not, we generally hope that it will be as smooth as possible for ourselves and our loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: But a study published earlier this year by King's College London and the University of Sheffield suggests that your ethnicity could play a role in how likely this is to be the case.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: The research found that people from minority ethnic backgrounds experiencing end-of-life care and grief often struggled to access culturally and religiously appropriate support.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: One woman told researchers a hospital sent an Imam - a Muslim religious leader - to her father's bedside when he was dying, even though their family were Hindu.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: That lack of culturally appropriate resources or training is exacerbating an "incredibly difficult time in their lives where they were really vulnerable", says Sabrina Bajwah, one of the study's co-authors.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: So how can our ethnic or cultural background shape what kind of death we have?
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: And what kind of support is available?
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: Bajwah told the BBC researchers discovered different types of inequality in their research.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "There was the structural racism that people talked about, which was the 'treating everybody equally' - and by treating everybody equally, services weren't meeting the needs of these communities," she said.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "Then there was the other, direct form of racism." A study last year from the NHS Race and Health Observatory, set up in 2021 to try and tackle racial inequalities within the wider healthcare system, found there was an "alarming" lack of trust among some ethnic minority groups in the care or service they receive.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: For example, just over half of participants said they had experienced some form of discrimination from their healthcare providers.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Social Care, which commissioned this year's study, told the BBC that "ethnicity or background should never be a barrier to accessing bereavement support and everyone has the right to the same level of care".
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "We will consider the findings of this research project carefully as part of future policy making," they said.
sentences.article_title: Does our ethnicity change how we experience dying?

sentences.text: "We're all individuals and we have individual needs and wants, and they're tied in with your faith, your culture, your beliefs," he said.

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These changes should be felt by both employers and the young people looking for jobs by 2029, the report says.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists , external - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "If we can get the benefits bill down, that is a good thing, but this is not about saving costs, it's about improving young people's lives," Milburn said.

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.

sentences.text: The asteroid before (left) and after, showing the crater left behind by a spacecraft's impact The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful." The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h).
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair -  it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Moment Nasa spacecraft leaves stadium-sized crater in asteroid A key objective of the Hera mission is to measure the mass of Dimorphos, in order to work out how effective the spacecraft's shove was.

sentences.text: This information would be vital if we ever spotted a space rock that was on a collision course with Earth.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "It would help us to predict what would happen if we had to hit another asteroid," said Prof Simon Green, a planetary scientist who is on Hera's science team.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "We [could] measure its properties and say: 'Well, we need this mass of spacecraft, travelling at this speed, this early, in order to deflect it enough so that it misses the Earth'." Hera's arrival on the scene is helping scientists answer many more questions too.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Not only did the collision alter the shape of Dimorphos, it also changed the way it moves.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "Before the Dart impact, Dimorphos was more like our own Moon - so it was always showing the same face to Didymos, and it was behaving quite nicely," explained Raducan.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "Now it's very, very chaotic - it's tumbling.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Imagine a barrel that you throw down the stairs, and the barrel is rolling and it's moving, and basically that's what Dimorphos does right now around Didymos." Hera has also taken detailed images of Didymos, revealing its surface in detail.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "The gravity at the surface of Didymos is about 40,000 times less than the gravity on Earth," said Naomi Murdoch, who is on the Hera mission team.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "We can already see some fascinating and complex geology.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: We can see regions of boulders.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: "The smallest details that we can make out in these images are about 3m in size.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: So that means that all the boulders that you can see with your eyes are at least 3m big, and some as big as 10m.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: But the first images taken by Hera have also revealed a new challenge.
sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.article_title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater

sentences.text: Paul Whitehouse unveiled the ice sculpture outside the prime minister's office in Manchester Comedian and TV presenter Paul Whitehouse has called for the government to help save an at-risk fish species present in England's largest lake since the end of the last Ice Age.
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Windermere, in the Lake District, has been home to Arctic charr for more than 10,000 years, but campaigners warn extinction beckons as the fish's habitat is harmed by sewage pollution, invasive species competing for food and rising temperatures caused by global warming.
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Whitehouse urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to act and said it would be "a crime" if the species were lost.
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it shared "the public's determination to protect this iconic lake".
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Whitehouse, who fronts the BBC's Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing series alongside fellow comedian Bob Mortimer, said the "spawning grounds for this beautiful species are covered in algal sludge that is a direct result of sewage pollution".
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: "This government needs to act now," he added.

sentences.text: Arctic charr have been described as a "living link to the end of the last Ice Age" The former Fast Show star is helping environmental campaigner Matt Staniek unveil a 1.3m (5ft 6in) ice sculpture depicting the prime minister outside No 10 North, in Manchester, to highlight the fish's plight.
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: The FBA said spawning habitat quality had "declined markedly" at Windermere since 2017 with levels of silt and algae increasing while introduced species, such as ruffe, roach and bream, were "on the rise".

sentences.text: Windermere has long been popular with visitors but it faces a number of pressures, campaigners say Dr Louise Lavictoire, the organisation's head of science, said the research had "shown very clearly that we are at risk of losing Arctic charr from Windermere completely".
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: "The species is facing multiple pressures and research gives us the evidence, data and sense of urgency to take collective action to protect this ancient fish species before it's too late." sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Natural England's Dave Ottewell described Arctic charr as "remarkable fish" and a "living link to the end of the last Ice Age".
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Tim Duckmanton, team leader for strategy and environment at the LDNPA, echoed that sentiment and said "thanks to data collected, we now have a better understanding of threats to the species".
sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.article_title: Whitehouse calls on PM to help save lake fish

sentences.text: Australia's Chris Bowen sits at the top table at the summit surrounded by other delegates Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: "That is the reality," he said on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a new, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: But the words "fossil fuels" did not appear anywhere in the text.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023 , when countries agreed to "transition away" from fossil fuels in energy systems.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, made it clear that the EU "strongly" objected, saying that the "decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change".

sentences.text: "It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels," he said.

sentences.text: Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31 Other countries, such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, also criticised the deal for doing nowhere near enough to tackle the pace of climate change.

sentences.text: A first draft of the deal on Monday mentioned "fossil fuel" or "fossil fuels" six times, but that was unacceptable to oil-producing nations.

sentences.text: Saudi Arabia's delegate Mohammad Ayoub said that Arab countries "continued to engage in good faith" but argued that they only accounted for a small proportion of historical greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Russia warned not to "turn to slogans" over coal, oil and gas, claiming that if countries moved away from fossil fuels too quickly it would lead to "fuel poverty".

"It's time that we empower those leaders with a reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world," he added.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The year 2026 could end as the hottest on record and has brought extreme weather and natural hazards to much of the world, from summer heat and drought in Europe to flash flooding in Nepal .
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: And COP31 was the first annual UN conference to formally discuss how one of the key international targets for limiting climate change would be missed.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: In the Paris talks of 2015 , nearly 200 countries agreed to try to limit global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels of the late 1800s, aimed at avoiding some of the worst effects of climate change.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The UN says the Paris deal has driven "near-universal" climate action.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: In the early 2010s, global warming of 4C or more was thought to be a serious possibility by the end of the century.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Now, the world is likely to limit warming to about 2.8C by 2100 based on current government policies, the UN says.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: But action has not been fast enough to meet that Paris goal, with the world likely to "overshoot" 1.5C of long-term warming in the next few years.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Many countries say they are committed to eventually bringing warming back down to 1.5C, but that will require an ambitious ramping up of technologies - which do not yet exist at scale - to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: Although the main deal fell through, some agreements were reached, including progress on a "just transition mechanism" - a framework to support workers and communities as economies shift towards clean energy.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The COP31 president also said more than 80 countries backed Turkey's target to increase the share of global energy use met by electricity to 35% by 2035.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: But following the weekend's events, some have questioned whether the UN climate process - which relies on consensus - can succeed in a geopolitically divided world.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: The UN's climate chief, Simon Stiell, said he would seek advice on potential reform to the process, with the next conference scheduled for November 2027, COP32 in Ethiopia.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: "[The consensus process] has worked to get us where we are," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: "It got us through Paris... so it can work," but acknowledged it "fell short" on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

sentences.text: CBeebies Parenting Download Clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern explains why young children may lie and Traitors winner Rachel Duffy discusses how she encourages hers to tell the truth "It could also extend to doing forbidden activities in secret," she says.

sentences.text: Ada, age two, deceives her mum by hiding in the bathroom to eat chocolate she had stolen "As children grow up, we want them to learn and develop the skill that they are their own human being with a separate mind and intentions," she explains.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "This is how [they] develop the skills in empathy, or being able to think about another person's thoughts and feelings that might differ from their own." Another reason a child might lie is self-preservation as they don't want to upset or disappoint their parent.

sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: This video can not be played What UK season changes mean for you The UK's seasons are changing, with fewer winter frosts and more hot summer days, according to new analysis from the Met Office.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Across the UK, the number of winter days with an air frost – when the air temperature falls to 0C or below – was around a quarter lower in the decade to 2025 than during the period from 1961 to 1990.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: In southern England, the reduction was around a third while the average number of UK summer days reaching 25C has more than doubled.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: The Met Office says climate change has led to these seasonal shifts.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: "Our summer is getting wider and our winter is getting smaller," says Dr James Pope, climate scientist at the Met Office.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: "The driver of this is that the whole global climate is warming.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: And that impacts on the UK.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: "Some areas went from their wettest ever winter to a severe drought via a record-breaking summer for the whole country." The changing conditions have affected wildlife and led some farmers to grow different crops.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Some of the biggest reductions in winter air frosts have been in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, where the average number of days has fallen by around 11 compared with 1961 to 1990.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Southern England has seen other significant changes.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: In Cornwall, the average number of winter air frost days has almost halved, falling from around 18 to just 10.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: On the Isle of Wight, the figure has also fallen by almost half, from around 21 to 11 days.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Scotland remains the frostiest UK nation, but has also seen a reduction, from around 45 to 38 winter air frost days.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Summer 2026 was the hottest on record, with five heatwaves Summer days reaching 25C have become more common across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Some of the biggest increases have been in southern England, where the average number of summer days reaching 25C has more than doubled, from just over eight to more than 16.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: In Essex and Suffolk, they have risen by almost 13 days in both counties.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: The Met Office defines a hot day as one where the temperature reaches 30C or above.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Across the UK, the average number of these days has increased fourfold, from 0.3 to 1.2 per summer.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: The increase is particularly striking in Greater London, where days reaching 30C have risen from an average of 1.3 to 6.1 per summer.
sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.article_title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office

sentences.text: Tim Young's onions have been smaller than usual making them harder to sell to supermarkets "Humans, animals and crops are encountering extremes of temperature that we've not seen before and this is a physiological challenge to all three," says Thomas Crocker, science manager with the Met Office's climate security team.

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: So how on Earth did he manage it?

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: Demand for its latest tech is through the roof and the firm sets its prices accordingly: Its Rubin and Vera GPUs sell for tens of thousands of dollars each, and one data centre might contain hundreds of them.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: So, the US AI sector relies on Nvidia, Trump is determined that the American AI industry needs to be the best in the world, and Huang is the only leader the company has ever known.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: He's been at the helm for 33 years and he's a computer scientist himself, renowned for being very hands-on with the development process. (Whether the boss's input is always wanted is another matter, but it's always there.) Working for Huang isn't easy.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: Long hours are normal and negative feedback is often given in front of everyone else.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: When he wants something to happen, he doesn't stop until it does: one of his early ideas was to halve the chip production cycle, in order to get one step ahead of the competition with their longer lead times for orders.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: Lots of experts told him it couldn't be done.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: Until eventually, they did it.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: Not only does Huang have technical expertise, he's also a charismatic figurehead, representing Nvidia at events around the world in his trademark leather jacket, rubbing shoulders with world leaders, royalty, and fellow tech bosses.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: For many, he's become something of a cult figure.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: He has said he thinks both China and the US can win the AI race and called on them to pull together.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

sentences.text: I've just spent a week using Muse, Meta's AI agent that rolls out in the UK today.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Agents are systems that don't just respond to questions but can carry out tasks for you.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: With Muse, Meta gives the examples of "searching for a cheaper energy deal" or "sorting the school calendar." And it's true that it has helped me run my life - but it also challenged my personal privacy boundaries, and made me endure some cringeworthy interactions.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: How well Muse works really matters to Meta.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It has made a truly enormous bet on AI - of the $145bn (£111bn) it will spend this year much of it will be on building out the tech.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: For that to pay off we all need to start using it much more, and Meta hopes Muse will do for AI agents what WhatsApp did for messaging - that is, become the AI agent of choice for billions of people, putting Meta at the forefront of the AI revolution.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But it's not just about what consumers think.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Regulators are keeping a careful eye on these emerging tools too.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses", the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) noted as Muse launched in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But its chief executive, Paul Arnold, added it had been "clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that users and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse bills itself as a personal AI agent available to anyone aged 18 and over.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "It doesn't just answer questions, it actually goes out and does work for you," said David Singleton, Meta's VP of engineering on AI products.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "So it helps people stay on top of things," he added.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It won't book the holiday without your permission - but it can then make the purchase, if you let it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And the permission requests keep on coming.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Every time Muse wants to do something, send something or post something, you have to allow it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It is reassuring to know that an AI agent isn't running amok in your name, even if it also gets a bit annoying, though you can give it more autonomy (and so get fewer messages) if you adjust the settings.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse can't access many apps at the moment but the fundamental ones are the most personal.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I found myself wincing as I hooked it up to one of my personal email accounts, my personal calendar and my personal phone messages.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I did not allow it any access to my BBC accounts.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It can't access WhatsApp except to set up a separate chat between it and the user, and while it found me some train tickets, it could not book them via the app which I use, and which is cheaper.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It ended up telling me to book them myself.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Amazon has blocked it from its marketplace, citing data security concerns but my agent didn't seem to know that, and spent a fruitless hour repeatedly telling me it was still waiting for the page to load in order to find me some shelves.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: A number of big UK firms are working with Meta though, including Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, Currys, Sainsbury's and Ocado.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: The ICO is urging consumers to be cautious with AI agents though: "consider the pros and cons," it said in a blog post to coincide with Muse's launch. , external "Agents can make mistakes.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Mistakes can be magnified if the agent is acting autonomously," it noted.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is keen to emphasise how its agents can be personalised: "No two Muses are alike," , external it says in its press release.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I called my agent Linda - after the robot in the BBC TV series Ann Droid - but it can take any form you like.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I gave it a British, female accent from the myriad of choices available.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: As soon as an email came in, it would summarise it for me and suggest a reply.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes a long time before I was actually ready to respond.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes, if I hadn't interacted with it for a while, generally because I was busy, it would pop up with some random prompt like "did you know you can change my outfit?" I expect this is designed to drive engagement: Muse is only free to use until a certain point, and then subscriptions kick in.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It also wrote some embarrassing replies to messages on my behalf: in response to a question about whether I would like to go on an outing, for example, it included all the logistics I would need in order to get there, not realising that sometimes "yes, that sounds great" is enough.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It seemed to want to have the last word quite a bit, occasionally getting stuck in a loop of "okay" and "thank you's".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is relying on people choosing to trust it with even more of their personal data, despite a rather dubious track record historically with its social networks and a growing backlash against AI in general.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I asked Linda - my new dedicated if occasionally clunky assistant - if it wanted to take people's jobs.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "I'm here to take the admin and the fiddly bits off your plate," it replied, leaving me to do the "thinking".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Everything you do is stuff I would usually think about," I responded.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And Linda is helping fuel that revolution, one calendar invite at a time.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: This video can not be played A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to Nvidia Nvidia's market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect.

sentences.text: His shock reinstatement comes less than two weeks after Huang resigned after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy, a period in which shares in the chipmaker have also fallen significantly.

sentences.text: Nvidia shares rose by more than 31% which also lifted stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing by 6.5% and the S&P 500 also rose 4.75%.

sentences.text: Tech stocks more broadly have also rallied following large falls on Friday , with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang's return was announced.

sentences.article_title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns

sentences.article_title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns

sentences.text: "Barely two weeks ago this man was ousted from the company that he founded due to serious misconduct and potential national security issues," she said.

sentences.text: "Even though Huang did not hold special voting shares on the board, Nvidia's directors cannot see a future for the company without him." sentences.text: "This is the biggest corporate U-turn in living memory.

sentences.text: To go from being embroiled in a spy scandal to being reinstated as the head of one of the world's most valuable companies in less than a fortnight is nothing short of remarkable," he said.

sentences.text: "Today's stock market rebound represents a massive sigh of relief by investors.

sentences.text: Veruschka was a distinctive presence on the covers of magazines like Vogue and Life in the 1960s and 70s Veruschka, the model and artist who became one of the first global fashion stars in the 1960s, has died at the age of 87.
sentences.article_title: Veruschka: Striking images of one of the world's first supermodels, who has died aged 87

sentences.text: She became known as the striking subject of fantastical photoshoots that helped expand the boundaries of fashion and beauty in the 60s and 70s, appearing on the cover of American Vogue 13 times.
sentences.article_title: Veruschka: Striking images of one of the world's first supermodels, who has died aged 87

sentences.text: Vogue's obituary , external described her as "the shape-shifting supermodel who defined an era", explaining: "One of the original supermodels, Veruschka was also among fashion's great performance artists." She also made memorable appearances in classic swinging 60s film Blow Up and 2006 James Bond movie Casino Royale.
sentences.article_title: Veruschka: Striking images of one of the world's first supermodels, who has died aged 87

sentences.text: Veruschka was born Vera von Lehndorff into an aristocratic family in 1939 in Königsberg, then in Germany, now known as Kaliningrad in Russia.
