sentences.text: Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: No company or chief executive has arguably been more consequential to the development of AI in recent years, with the US microchip manufacturer under Huang positioning itself as a critical cog in the development of the world-changing technology.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: That central position prompted questions, in the aftermath of Huang's departure over revelations of extramarital affairs, over how important he was to the wider AI industry and US economy.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The fact he has been handed his job back after just 11 days in a U-turn by Nvidia's board implies the top brass believe Huang is irreplaceable.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Shares in the company have surged on the news of Huang's shock return, following a period of sharp declines.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: While Nvidia is not as much of a household name as other Big Tech players such as Apple, Amazon and Microsoft, the company has been just as integral to the booming US stock market of recent years.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The billions of dollars being funnelled into AI and the construction of data centres has bolstered the American economy, with Nvidia being one of the biggest spenders.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Originally focusing on chips which process graphics for computer games, it pivoted to making the chips used in AI systems and now dominates the market.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: It is now one the most valuable firms in the world and its rapid growth is poised to continue as the firm's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Huang played a major role in the company, leading its shift towards AI, and maintained a firm grip on it, with up to 200 people directly reporting to him.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Some suggested his departure, which was sparked by the emergence that Huang had an affair with a woman alleged to have been a spy for China, posed a risk to the wider AI industry.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: That was because it was unclear whether Nvidia would change strategy and potentially rein in spending - a move could have had wider implications for the US economy, but which looks unlikely now Huang has returned.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The fears were sparked due to Nvidia being a key source of finance for many firms, as well as being a microchip supplier.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: On its journey to the top of the AI industry, it has, through Huang, created a spider's web of deals through what is known as "circular financing".
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Not only does it sell microchips to its customers, which include the likes of Meta, SpaceX and OpenAI, it has also provided funds for them and other firms in the supply chain by either handing out loans or investing in them directly.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The practice has prompted concerns among some investors, who worry what might happen if Nvidia were to turn off the spending taps.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: If investment dried up, would other firms in the supply chain cut spending or jobs themselves?
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Would that spread to the wider US economy?
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: That risk was perhaps why tech bosses including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the CEO of Fortnite maker Epic Games, had called for Huang's reinstatement.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation, and backed a campaign, along with shareholders and supporters, to "Bring Jensen Back".
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Following the announcement of Huang's return, Musk posted: "The mistake has been corrected." Kathleen Brooks, research director at investment platform XTB, said Huang's return suggested he was "the godfather" of AI and has the status to shift "the dial for corporate finance".
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: "Is Jensen Huang the most valuable man on the planet?
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: His return suggests more of the same when it comes to circular financing and the rapid AI infrastructure build out, and the market loves it," she added.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: However, Huang's return to Nvidia does not solve the wider issues rattling the tech stock markets in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Investors had taken fright at Democrat gains in the US midterm elections, with many having campaigned for tougher regulation of AI firms.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Questions also remain about whether the huge sums being invested in AI will actually pay off.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: However, investment in AI is still expected to exceed $1 trillion in 2026, according to investment bank Goldman Sachs, who said the technology would remain the "dominant driver of business investment growth" next year.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The value of the shares in Big Tech companies have cushioned the US economy from global economic shocks, including tariffs, buoying investments and pensions for people worldwide.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: President Donald Trump hailed Huang as a "great patriot and national treasure" after his reappointment and pointed to the chief executive's wider impact.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: "The country needs Jensen's leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy," he wrote on Truth Social.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Nvidia said its leadership had received input from "senior levels of the United States government and was "confident that Mr Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk".
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Two supporters of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) interrupted the event hosted by Sir Paul Smith at Nottingham's Broadway Cinema on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: The protest follows investigations by PETA into alleged animal cruelty at mohair production facilities in South Africa and Lesotho, including one it said had links to a Paul Smith supplier.

sentences.text: The company said it upheld the highest standards of animal welfare across its supply chain.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: PETA has called on the brand to stop using mohair in its clothing Mohair is a fibre made from the hair of Angora goats and is commonly used in clothing.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: Smith said all its mohair was certified under the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS) and that it would take relevant action if suppliers were found to be in breach of its animal welfare standards.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Paul Smith said: "At Paul Smith, we uphold the highest standards of animal welfare across our supply chain, and all our suppliers are required to adhere to these standards.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: "Every batch of mohair used by Paul Smith is certified to the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS), the internationally recognised standard for responsible mohair production.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: "If there is evidence that a supplier has not upheld these standards, we will take appropriate action in line with our ethical commitments." PETA said its investigators had filmed goats being injured during shearing, including  at mohair facilities under the RMS.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: Allen said: "Hundreds of fashion brands have already ditched mohair, and Paul Smith must do the right thing and follow suit.
sentences.article_title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk

sentences.text: "PETA also urges shoppers to do their part by leaving cruelty on the rack and opting for animal-free materials such as cotton, hemp and bamboo." Other brands, such as Helmut Lang, G-Star, Gap, Fred Perry, Barbour, UNIQLO, and Zara, have already banned mohair.

sentences.text: "I really love this space, it just makes me smile every time I come in - it's actually joyful," she says.

sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Another wall has remnants of London's former greyhound tracks.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: DJ Ralph Lawson rediscovered a tape that Daft Punk gifted him in 1997 Daft Punk have become household names after storming the charts with One More Time and Get Lucky - with an intimate set in 1990s Leeds lingering in the memories of attendees.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Now, those recollections have been reignited by the discovery of a lost mix by the French electronic duo hidden for several decades.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It all started when I opened a show for Daft Punk in 1997," says Ralph Lawson, standing on the top floor of the Mint XL club in the city centre.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: The 2,500-capacity venue is empty aside from staff testing out a staggering number of lights, bouncing off the spotless floors.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: It is a far cry from Ralph's first clubs when he started DJing back in 1991.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He is a co-founding resident DJ at the legendary Back to Basics club - a DIY house music event that became one of Europe's longest-running club nights, hosting global stars until sunrise.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Mint evolved from an intimate Leeds club into festivals, large-scale productions and the new Mint XL club Ralph is holding up a digital audio tape (DAT) - a discontinued method of recording high quality audio.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: On its side are the handwritten words: "Daft Punk Mix Feb '97." "Daft Punk got so big so quickly, they were on such big stages at festivals that they did not really DJ," remembers the music producer.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "That is what makes the tape rare." The French pair were rapidly rising to fame when they were booked for Back to Basics, but they were pipped to the headline slot by drum and bass pioneer Goldie.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Daft Punk were on their rapid rise to stardom when they visited Leeds in 1997, but did not top the bill By the time the night arrived, Ralph recalls "there were queues around the block".
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Despite accidentally jogging one of their records during the set, Ralph got on well with both Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo - even if the latter only uttered a few words to him.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I would not say I was best mates with them, but I could get on a guest list," says Ralph.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Whatever their relationship, it was strong enough that Daft Punk sent Ralph a gift in the post - an hour-long mixtape for his radio show on Kiss 105 FM.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: This is the only picture Ralph has of Daft Punk playing their DJ set in Leeds After it was played out on air, Ralph forgot about its existence for decades.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He finally rediscovered it during a root around in some old storage boxes, but there was a problem.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It immediately ripped," he says.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I took it out and there were two bits of tape hanging out." Despite being in a dry studio, mould had found its way in.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: When Ralph tried to play the tape it immediately ripped Spurred on by his social media followers begging for him to salvage the mix, Ralph found a company that preserves tapes in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "The problem with DAT is that it is incredibly fragile," says Adrian Finn, from  Greatbear, one of the people tasked with fixing the broken tape.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He estimates the team spent hours across multiple weeks on this "difficult job", carefully disassembling the tape, repairing the rips and getting rid of the mould.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It's nice to make people happy through this kind of restoration work," says Adrian, who admits he was dancing around "a little bit" while listening back to the mix.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I thought it was good and glad it played back with hardly any errors." Adrian Finn from Greatbear in Bristol was one of the people tasked with fixing the mixtape Back at Mint XL in Leeds, Ralph cannot help but grin as he recounts attempting to play the mix for a second time.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I was literally floored," he laughs, toppling over in delight once the kick drum blasted out of his speakers.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Ralph had no idea what the first track of the hour-long mix would be, so when it was one of his favourites - Everybody Dancing by the late American DJ Romanthony - he knew it would be "very special".
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Ralph dropped to the floor in celebration when he heard the tape for the first time It is the "rawness" of the vinyl mix - complete with crackles and impressive manual transitions - that Ralph adores.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It's a testament to the times," he says.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "Not as polished as things are now, where people can see precisely how in time they are and have visual cues." While the discovery may be a success for the nostalgia and memories of 1990s clubbing, Ralph also hopes the tape and the meaning behind it will inspire the next generation of DJs, music curators and artists.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I want them to think, 'I could get behind the decks or find the next Daft Punk and put them on at our night', and there's the space for them to do that in Leeds." Will another French electronic music duo stop by in Leeds on their way to global stardom?
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Somali government is facing political crises and rebellions, creating vulnerabilities al-Shabab could exploit, he adds.

sentences.text: There's another reason some jihadists may see an opportunity to expand: they believe Western governments have bigger fish to fry.

sentences.text: With the war in Ukraine, US-Iran conflict in the Middle East and growing rivalries with China and Russia, fighting jihadists is no longer the priority it was after 9/11.
sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: The US withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021 and the Taliban's return to power, followed by Sharaa's rise in Syria, have reinforced that belief.

sentences.text: The Taliban has inspired many jihadists Colin Clarke, executive director of the Soufan Center, a non-profit research group that focuses on security, says some jihadist groups have learnt that avoiding confrontation with the US can help them escape Western military action and "live to fight another day".
sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: But history offers a warning.
sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: After the 2011 Arab uprisings, which largely sidelined al-Qaeda, affiliated jihadist groups in Yemen, Libya and Tunisia began using the name Ansar al-Sharia (Supporters of Sharia) to win local support without carrying the al-Qaeda brand.
sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: But not everyone is changing tactics.
sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.article_title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?

sentences.text: And it's too early to say whether groups like JNIM and al-Shabab will follow the Taliban or Syrian examples, and whether they're willing to make compromises.

sentences.text: Some jihadist groups may become more focused on local politics as they face the challenges of governing.

sentences.text: Nearly a decade of fighting in Cameroon has left countless lives shattered.

sentences.text: The crisis began in October 2016, when lawyers and teachers in Cameroon's English-speaking regions went on strike over the alleged marginalisation of Anglophone communities by the Francophone-dominated government.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: They were concerned about the appointment of French-speaking judges and teachers to courts and schools in the English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Initially, the protest was peaceful, with thousands demanding greater recognition of the English-speaking minority.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: But human rights groups accused security forces of using excessive force to suppress the protests.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: The crackdown, critics say, helped fuel an armed separatist movement.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: By 2017, a dozen armed groups had emerged, according to the International Crisis Group, seeking independence for the two English-speaking regions and the creation of a breakaway state known as Ambazonia.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Since then, separatist fighters have engaged in a prolonged and often brutal conflict with government forces.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Rights groups have documented serious abuses by both sides.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Separatist fighters have been accused of targeted killings, kidnappings for ransom, torture and attacks on schools and other public and private facilities.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Government forces, meanwhile, have faced allegations of arbitrary arrests and detention, torture and unlawful killings.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Both sides have denied the accusations, although in some instances they have acknowledged responsibility for abuses.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: The violence has devastated communities and forced nearly half a million people from their homes, according to data published by the UN this year.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: At least 6,000 people have been killed since the conflict began, according to Human Rights Watch.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, says more than 70,000 Cameroonians have sought refuge in neighbouring Nigeria.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Gloria Akom is among 15,000 people who fled Cameroon for Nigeria's Cross River state Glory Akom, 44, lives with a disability after surviving severe burns in an incident unrelated to the conflict.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: The mother-of-two now lives in a camp in Ogoja, a town in Nigeria's south-eastern Cross River state, near the Cameroonian border.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Ogoja hosts about 15,000 refugees across three settlements, Richard Effiong, from the UNHCR, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: The UNHCR has provided refugees with brick houses topped with tin roofs.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: For many, however, uncertainty remains over when, or whether, they will ever return home.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: Glory says her life in Cameroon was far better.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: She ran a business and was able to provide for her family.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: But everything changed when fighting intensified in 2017.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: She said soldiers deployed to her area in the Southwest region pursued residents into the bush, forcing them to abandon their homes and flee into Nigeria.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: "We were sleeping in the bush, as we were always running," she said.
sentences.article_title: Shot in the face at 15: The lives shattered by Cameroon's decade of conflict

sentences.text: "If you slept in your house, they could kill you there." Initially, she settled in a neighbouring village before moving to Ogoja, where she was eventually allocated a permanent home.

sentences.text: Like many other refugees, Glory depends on $67 (£51) monthly cash assistance from UNHCR to support her children, one of who suffers from sickle cell and requires regular medical attention.

sentences.text: Some analysts argue that the conflict has persisted for so long partly because of the government's failure to address the grievances that triggered it.
